subject: ACME bake-off plan & next steps
messages:
From: marissa_cole@redwood.ai
To: alex.johnson@acme.com, sana.patel@acme.com
Cc: aditya_rao@redwood.ai, vanessa_ortiz@redwood.ai
Date: 2026-04-12T09:15:00-07:00
Subject: ACME bake-off plan & next steps

Alex / Sana  thanks again for the demo this morning. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we stay aligned as you run a competitive evaluation: 

Recap: 
- You asked for a side-by-side comparison vs the hyperscalers (AWS/GCP) and two inference API providers you mentioned on the call.
- Key success criteria you shared: 99th percentile latency under 300ms for conversational flows, consistent output quality (no regressions vs your current prompts), predictable cost per 1k tokens, and SOC2 evidence for procurement.

Redwood differentiators to highlight (short):
- Unified runtime across hosted/dedicated/private with production SLOs and routing policies (helps with predictable latency).
- Intelligent batching + prefix caching to reduce per-token cost for conversational workloads.
- Transparent perf profiles and cost estimates by model + quantization profiles.

Proposed bake-off plan (high level):
1) Security & procurement items (this week): get ACME's security questionnaire and any required attestation docs. Owner: Marissa (I'll coordinate).
2) Technical smoke tests (by 2026-04-16): Aditya to run the provided prompt set against Redwood + 2 competitors for basic latency/throughput. Deliverable: runtimes_cost_estimate.csv + raw traces. Owner: Aditya.
3) Quality/regression evals (by 2026-04-20): Vanessa to run ACME prompt/test set and compute automatic evals (BLEU/embedding-similarity + manual spot checks). Deliverable: bakeoff_test_plan.xlsx + qualitative notes. Owner: Vanessa.
4) Final bake-off report (by 2026-04-23): consolidated results, recommended model configuration and cost/latency tradeoffs. Owner: Marissa.

Success criteria (first pass):
- 99p latency < 300ms for 2k token session (or clearly documented tradeoff if batching needed)
- <10% quality delta vs ACME's current baseline on core prompts
- Total cost per 1M tokens <= threshold we discuss in the proposal document

Attachments: please see the security questionnaire placeholder (if you have a PDF/XLS, please send). I'll attach an initial test plan for Aditya/Vanessa once we align.

Next steps for you:
- Share the completed security questionnaire (or confirm SOC2 report preferred doc)
- Share the canonical prompt/test set and a sample production trace if available
- Confirm target timeline (are these dates OK?)

Thanks  happy to jump back on a quick call if you want to walk through the plan.

 Marissa
Marissa Cole
Enterprise Sales
Redwood Inference
marissa_cole@redwood.ai
From: alex.johnson@acme.com
To: marissa_cole@redwood.ai
Cc: sana.patel@acme.com
Date: 2026-04-12T11:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: ACME bake-off plan & next steps

Thanks Marissa  this is great and aligns to what we discussed. Quick notes/questions: 

1) We can get the security questionnaire back to you today (sending with this thread).
2) For the quality/regression step: when you say "<10% quality delta", can you confirm the metric you prefer? We typically look at embedding-similarity on answer-level and then manual spot checks.
3) On latency: our current baseline is 99p = ~250ms on our infra for 1.2k avg tokens; we will include sample traces.

One more ask: can you include AWS/GCP as part of the technical smoke tests? We're running a parallel eval internally and want apples-to-apples comparisons.

Attachments: ACME_Security_Questionnaire.xlsx (attached)

Alex
Alex Johnson
Head of Platform Engineering
Acme Corp
From: marissa_cole@redwood.ai
To: aditya_rao@redwood.ai, vanessa_ortiz@redwood.ai, jonas_weber@redwood.ai
Date: 2026-04-12T13:22:00-07:00
Subject: Fwd: ACME bake-off plan & next steps

Folks  forwarding ACME's questionnaire and notes. Action items below: 

- Aditya: please scope the smoke tests to include Redwood, AWS (Bedrock endpoint), and GCP (Vertex). Use the attached prompt set when Alex sends it; aim for raw latency traces (p95/p99), avg token throughput, and cost estimate by model. Timeline: start this week, initial results by 2026-04-16.
- Vanessa: build the eval plan for quality (automatic + manual). We'll target the <10% delta goal but capture per-test metrics so we can show where differences occur. Deliverables: bakeoff_test_plan.xlsx and a one-pager for the AE deck. Timeline: drafts by 2026-04-20.
- Jonas: can you join Aditya for the infra runbook (credentials, region selection, and any rate limit keys)?

Please add any caveats (e.g., quantization differences, model families to compare). I'll coordinate with Alex on procurement items and compile the final report.

 Marissa
From: aditya_rao@redwood.ai
To: marissa_cole@redwood.ai, vanessa_ortiz@redwood.ai, jonas_weber@redwood.ai
Date: 2026-04-13T09:04:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Fwd: ACME bake-off plan & next steps

Thanks  plan sounds good. Quick clarifications and proposed test matrix: 

Test matrix (proposed):
- Models: Redwood-base-gtp-13b-quant, AWS-xyz-13b, GCP-abc-13b (match sizes where possible)
- Payloads: ACME prompt set (30 queries across conversational + document QA flows)
- Concurrency: low-latency (1 concurrent request) and bursty (10 concurrent) runs
- Metrics: p50/p95/p99 latency, tokens/sec, per-token cost (using list pricing + observed throughput), memory/KV cache hit rate where applicable

Success criteria mapping: 
- Latency: p99 < 300ms (if not, document batching needed and show per-token cost tradeoff)
- Quality: embedding-similarity >= 0.9 avg on core prompts (we'll compute cosine similarity on response embeddings)

I'll stand up the harness in our staging org and request AWS/GCP endpoints from Jonas so we can run simultaneously. ETA: initial raw results by 2026-04-16 EOD. I'll attach the runtimes_cost_estimate.csv once the initial run completes.

Note: quantized variants will likely lower latency/cost but may affect quality  we'll include both full-precision and quantized runs where feasible.

 Aditya
Senior Solutions Engineer
Redwood Inference

Thanks  looking forward to getting you clear apples-to-apples data.

 Marissa
